ns2:section.sectionText: This course examines the role of photography in public contexts and engages such questions as: How do photographs participate in public deliberation about social and political issues? How does photographic rhetoric shape who we imagine ourselves to be as citizens? In what ways has photography historically been used to intervene in public debate? How does the contemporary public engage photography today? Specific topics include war, civil rights, labor, documentary, environment, portraiture, trauma/violence, and politics. We will also discuss the changing nature of photography in the digital age (e.g., cell phone photography and social media).
